title: For better or for worse: the race where Finnish men carry their wives

sents.en: Every summer, a sleepy town in central Finland plays host to one of the world's oddest sporting events.
sents.zh: 每年夏天，芬兰中部一个安静的小镇都会举办一项全世界最古怪的体育赛事。

sents.en: The rules are simple, the prize is beer, and nobody takes it entirely seriously.
sents.zh: 规则很简单，奖品是啤酒，而且没有人完全把它当回事。

sents.en: Sonkajärvi, a town of a few thousand people, is not an obvious place to stage a world championship.
sents.zh: 松卡耶尔维是个只有几千人的小镇，按理说不像是举办世界锦标赛的地方。

sents.en: Yet each July thousands of visitors descend on it to watch men sprint through mud with a woman slung over their shoulders.
sents.zh: 然而每年七月，成千上万的游客涌向这里，看男人们肩上扛着一个女人在泥地里飞奔。

sents.en: The sport, known in Finnish as eukonkanto, has been held there since 1992.
sents.zh: 这项运动芬兰语叫 eukonkanto（背妻），从 1992 年起就在这里举办。

sents.en: Its origins, supposedly, lie in the 19th century.
sents.zh: 据说它的起源可以追溯到 19 世纪。

sents.en: Local folklore tells of a robber called Herkko Rosvo-Ronkainen, who is said to have tested would-be members of his gang by making them carry heavy sacks through the forest.
sents.zh: 当地民间传说讲到一个叫赫尔科·罗斯沃-龙凯宁的强盗，据说他会让想入伙的人背着沉重的麻袋穿过森林，以此考验他们。

sents.en: Darker versions of the tale have his men raiding nearby villages and running off with women.
sents.zh: 这个故事更阴暗的版本说，他的手下会袭击附近的村子，把女人抢走。

sents.en: Whether any of this happened is anyone's guess; the town is happy to cash in on the legend either way.
sents.zh: 这些事有没有发生过，谁也说不准；不管怎样，小镇都乐于借这个传说赚钱。

sents.en: Historians may scoff, but a good story has never hurt tourism.
sents.zh: 历史学家也许会嗤之以鼻，但一个好故事从来不会对旅游业有坏处。

sents.en: The course is 253.5 metres long and features two dry obstacles and a water pit about a metre deep.
sents.zh: 赛道长 253.5 米，有两个陆地障碍和一个大约一米深的水坑。

sents.en: The "wife" does not have to be married to the carrier, or, indeed, to anyone.
sents.zh: 这位“妻子”不一定要和背她的人结婚，事实上，她跟谁结没结婚都无所谓。

sents.en: She must, however, be over 17 and weigh at least 49kg; anyone lighter is weighed down with a rucksack of ballast to make up the difference.
sents.zh: 不过，她必须年满 17 岁，体重至少 49 公斤；不够重的人要背一个装着配重的背包，把差的重量补上。

sents.en: Most teams opt for the so-called Estonian carry, in which the wife hangs upside down with her legs around the man's neck and her arms clasped around his waist.
sents.zh: 大多数队伍选择所谓的“爱沙尼亚背法”：妻子头朝下倒挂，双腿勾住男人的脖子，双臂紧紧抱住他的腰。

sents.en: It looks undignified, but it frees up the carrier's hands and keeps the weight close to his back.
sents.zh: 这姿势看起来很不体面，但它能空出背人者的双手，让重量紧贴他的后背。

sents.en: Estonian couples were so good at it that they dominated the event for much of the 2000s.
sents.zh: 爱沙尼亚的情侣们太擅长这个了，在 2000 年代的大部分时间里都称霸这项赛事。

sents.en: The winners take home the wife's weight in beer, which makes a heavier partner a burden on the course but a bonus on the podium.
sents.zh: 冠军能带走和妻子体重一样重的啤酒，所以重一点的搭档在赛道上是负担，到了领奖台上却成了福利。

sents.en: Many entrants turn up in fancy dress, cheer each other on and fall into the water pit with gusto.
sents.zh: 很多参赛者穿着奇装异服来，互相加油打气，还兴高采烈地摔进水坑里。

sents.en: Yet the top contenders train for months, because shaving a second off their time can mean the difference between glory and a long, wet walk home.
sents.zh: 然而顶尖的选手会训练好几个月，因为把成绩缩短一秒，就可能是荣耀和湿漉漉地走回家之间的差别。

sents.en: The idea has spread: similar races are now held in America and Britain, among other places.
sents.zh: 这个点子已经传开了：美国、英国等地现在也会举办类似的比赛。

sents.en: Some purists complain that the spin-offs miss the point.
sents.zh: 一些较真的人抱怨说，这些衍生比赛没抓住重点。

sents.en: The point, the organisers insist, is not really about winning at all; it is about letting your hair down in a country often stereotyped as quiet and reserved.
sents.zh: 组织者坚持说，重点根本不在于输赢，而在于放松一下，尤其是在一个常被认为安静又内敛的国家。
